title: Detergent Utility for E. coli Membrane Protein Extraction and Delipidation
author: Wycisk, Urner
materials:
Timing: 1 week
1.Preparation of Agar plates.a.Mix ingredients for agar plates and autoclave the mixture.b.Let the solution cool down to 40°C.c.Add 100 μL of ampicillin stock.d.Pour autoclaved mixture into petri dishes and let the plates dry for 5 min.
Note: The mixture of ingredients for agar plates is sufficient for 6 plates.
2.Transform plasmid encoding ampicillin resistance and His-tagged AqpZ-GFP into C43(DE3) E. coli cells.a.Add 1 μL of plasmid solution (concentration = 100 ng/μL) to a 50 μL aliquot of commercially available C43 (DE3) E. coli suspension in a sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.b.Incubate the mixture on ice for 30 min.c.Heat shock the mixture in a warm water bath at 42°C for 45 s.d.Cool the mixture on ice for 2 min.e.Add 450 μL of starter culture medium.f.Shake the mixture with 180 rpm at 37°C for 1 h.g.Spread 50 μL of the mixture on an agar plate with a L-shaped cell spreader.h.Store agar plate in an incubator at 37°C for 16 h.i.Proceed with step 3 if individual colonies are visible on agar.3.Express target membrane protein AqpZ-GFP in C43(DE) E. coli cells.a.Add 5 μL of ampicillin stock to 5 mL of starter culture medium.b.Transfer five colonies from agar plate into 5 mL of starter culture medium.c.Shake starter culture medium with 180 rpm at 37°C for 8 h.d.Add 400 μL of ampicillin stock to 400 mL overnight culture medium.e.Transfer starter culture medium into 400 mL of overnight culture medium.f.Shake overnight culture medium with 180 rpm at 37°C for 16 h.g.Add 12 mL of ampicillin stock to 12 L of expression medium.h.Transfer overnight culture medium into 12 L of expression medium.i.Shake expression medium with 180 rpm at 37°C until an OD600 between 0.7 and 1.0 is reached.j.Add 12 mL of the isopropyl-ß-D-thiogalactopyranoside stock solution to 12 L of expression medium.k.Shake expression medium with 180 rpm at 37°C for 4 h.l.Centrifuge expression medium (5,000 × g for 10 min) and discard supernatant.m.Add 2 Roche protease inhibitor tablets to 100 mL suspension buffer.n.Homogenize cell pellets in 100 mL suspension buffer.4.Prepare membrane suspensions.a.Lyse cells by passing them four times through a Microfluidizer with an operating pressure of 1,500 bar and at a temperature of 4°C.b.Clarify supernatant by centrifugation (20,000 × g at 4°C for 20 min).c.Isolate and centrifuge supernatant (125,000 × g at 4°C for 45 min).d.Discard the supernatant.e.Add 1 Roche protease inhibitor tablet to 50 mL suspension buffer.f.Homogenize membrane pellet with 10 mL suspension buffer.g.Separate membrane suspension into 2 mL aliquots.h.Flash freeze 2 mL membrane suspension aliquots in liquid nitrogen.i.Store for up to 2 years at −80°C.

steps.title: Prepare agar plates
steps.instruction: Mix agar ingredients, autoclave, cool to 40 °C, add 100 µL ampicillin stock, pour into petri dishes, dry 5 min (sufficient for 6 plates).

steps.title: Transform plasmid into C43(DE3) cells
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL plasmid (100 ng/µL) to 50 µL C43(DE3) cells in a 1.5 mL tube, ice 30 min, heat‑shock 42 °C 45 s, ice 2 min, add 450 µL starter medium, shake 180 rpm 37 °C 1 h, spread 50 µL on agar plate, incubate 37 °C 16 h, proceed when colonies visible.

steps.title: Express His‑tagged AqpZ‑GFP
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL ampicillin stock to 5 mL starter medium, transfer five colonies into 5 mL starter medium, shake 180 rpm 37 °C 8 h; add 400 µL ampicillin stock to 400 mL overnight medium, transfer starter culture, shake 180 rpm 37 °C 16 h; add 12 mL ampicillin stock to 12 L expression medium, transfer overnight culture, shake 180 rpm 37 °C until OD₆₀₀ = 0.7‑1.0; add 12 mL IPTG stock to 12 L expression medium, shake 180 rpm 37 °C 4 h; centrifuge 5,000×g 10 min, discard supernatant, add 2 Roche protease‑inhibitor tablets to 100 mL suspension buffer, homogenize cell pellets in 100 mL suspension buffer.

steps.title: Prepare membrane suspension and aliquots
steps.instruction: Lyse cells by passing four times through a Microfluidizer at 1,500 bar, 4 °C; clarify supernatant 20,000×g 4 °C 20 min; isolate membranes by centrifugation 125,000×g 4 °C 45 min, discard supernatant; add 1 Roche protease‑inhibitor tablet to 50 mL suspension buffer; homogenize membrane pellet with 10 mL suspension buffer; aliquot into 2 mL portions, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂, store at –80 °C up to 2 years.

steps.title: Prepare buffer and detergent stock solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare extraction, wash and elute buffers as described in Materials; make elute buffer by mixing 9 parts wash buffer (18 mL) with 1 part elute buffer (2 mL) for 20 mL (adjust volume for number of detergents). Prepare hybrid detergent stock 10 % w/v (10 mg/mL) in MilliQ, agitate 20‑25 °C 16 h, store 4 °C up to 12 months (use highest possible w% if solubility lower). Prepare DDM and C8E4 stock solutions identically.

steps.title: Prepare ammonium acetate buffer for nMS
steps.instruction: Make ammonium acetate buffer per Materials; add 7 µL hybrid detergent stock (10 mg/mL) and 1,993 µL 200 mM ammonium acetate to reach 420 µM hybrid detergent in 2 mL total; store 4 °C up to 1 week. If cac unknown, determine it first.

steps.title: Make detergent‑containing wash and elution buffers
steps.instruction: Hybrid‑detergent wash buffer: add 17 µL hybrid detergent stock to 4,983 µL wash buffer (total 5 mL) → 420 µM. Hybrid‑detergent elute buffer: same volumes with elute buffer. Hybrid‑detergent wash‑elute buffer: add 34 µL stock to 9,966 µL wash‑elute buffer (total 10 mL) → 420 µM. Store all at 4 °C up to 1 week. Prepare analogous buffers with DDM and C8E4.

steps.title: Solubilize membranes and extract protein
steps.instruction: Cool all buffers on ice. In a tube combine 900 µL extraction buffer, 100 µL hybrid detergent stock (10 % w/v) and 100 µL membrane suspension; invert to mix; incubate on ice 10 min; centrifuge 12,000×g 4 °C 5 min to obtain clarified supernatant.

steps.title: Set up Ni‑NTA IMAC columns
steps.instruction: Agitate Ni‑NTA agarose to a homogeneous suspension; add 800 µL agarose suspension to each empty spin column; remove bottom caps, apply fingertip pressure to start flow; add 1 mL detergent‑containing wash buffer, let flow through; apply fingertip pressure again to accelerate flow.

steps.title: Perform IMAC purification and elution
steps.instruction: Load clarified supernatant onto columns (no pressure). Wash sequentially with 1 mL wash buffer then 4 mL wash‑elute buffer; discard flowthrough. Elute proteins with 400 µL elute buffer; collect eluate.

steps.title: Quantify protein by absorbance
steps.instruction: Transfer eluate to a 1 cm pathlength polystyrene cuvette and measure absorbance at 485 nm. If A₄₈₅ < 0.1, concentrate sample using a 0.5 mL Amicon filter (MWCO < protein MW) at 12,000×g 4 °C 5 min, record final volume, measure absorbance with a micro‑volume spectrophotometer, apply volume correction (divide each sample volume by the largest volume, multiply by its absorbance), then plot corrected A₄₈₅ versus detergent. Mark any detergent that yields unstable protein (precipitation) with an asterisk.

steps.title: Freeze and store protein samples
steps.instruction: Freeze eluates in liquid nitrogen, store at –80 °C up to 6 months; thaw on ice before use.

description: Detergents can be used to extract proteins from membranes. Whether it be commercially available or newly synthesized detergents, this protocol gives you a step-by-step analysis on how to test the utility of detergents for the extraction and delipidation of E. coli membrane proteins. Before starting with the protocol, detergents must be synthesized and purified. This protocol describes the use of a previously synthesized detergent, herein labeled as “hybrid detergent.” The hybrid detergent was purified by HPLC, and its structure was confirmed by NMR spectroscopy and high-resolution mass spectrometry. Further information on the synthesis and purification of the hybrid detergent can be found in this publication.1 Since this protocol aims for the assessment of the relative utilities of detergents for membrane protein purification, data will be compared with reference detergents. The aim of the here-chosen hybrid detergent example was to understand how combining the head groups of n-dodecyl-ß-D-maltoside (DDM) and tetraethylene glycol monooctyl ether (C8E4) into a hybrid detergent affects relative yields and delipidation obtainable from E. coli membrane proteins upon extraction and affinity purification.1 Therefore, DDM and C8E4 were included as commercially available references in this protocol. This protocol also includes an experiment for the determination of the minimum information required from a detergent to test its utility for membrane protein purification and analysis: the critical aggregation concentration (cac).2 The cac is the minimum concentration of a detergent required to form aggregates in solution.
